label: corelink-adapter-inline-ports-mandate
content: CoreLink adapters must declare adapter-local port traits (e.g. `pub trait CasStore`, `pub trait TenantResolver`) in their own `src/ports.rs` rather than importing workspace SPI. The canonical rationale lives in `specs/_proposals/adapters/README.md` §"Architectural pattern — inline-ports". Adapters do NOT import `corelink_cas::CasStore`, `corelink_auth::TenantResolver`, or `corelink_handler_cas::*`.
quote: Declare adapter-local `pub trait CasStore` + `pub trait TenantResolver` in `crates/corelink-adapter-cargo/src/ports.rs`

label: corelink-workspace-spi-traits-fictional
content: The workspace SPI trait names some adapter contracts reference (corelink_cas::CasStore, corelink_auth::TenantResolver, corelink_handler_cas::CasReadHandler/CasWriteHandler) are not needed by adapters, and some do not exist as named in the workspace. The v1 cargo packet HALTed pre-mutation on these fictional trait surfaces.
quote: None of these are needed; some don't exist as named.

label: corelink-audit-before-mutation
content: In CoreLink adapters, an audit event must be emitted BEFORE every state mutation (e.g. one event before each CAS put). This is a fail-closed chokepoint.
quote: Audit emit BEFORE every state mutation

label: corelink-loc-cap-l210
content: CoreLink rule L2.10: no `.rs` file may exceed 500 LOC (hard cap), with a sweet spot of ≤200 LOC per file.

label: corelink-rust-safety-conventions
content: CoreLink adapter crates must mark every pub type `#[non_exhaustive]`, set `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, and have zero `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` in `src/`. PATs must use `SecretString` plus `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` for comparison.

label: corelink-axum-version-alignment
content: CoreLink pins axum 0.7 with tower + http 1.x because that stack aligns with tonic 0.12 (which uses hyper 1 underneath). axum is configured default-features=false with features ["http1", "tokio", "json"].
quote: axum 0.7 + tower + http 1.x align with tonic 0.12 (hyper 1 underneath).

label: corelink-reqwest-rustls-config
content: CoreLink's workspace reqwest dependency is `reqwest = { version = "0.12", features = ["json", "rustls-tls"], default-features = false }` — rustls (not native-tls) is the TLS backend.

label: corelink-pat-constant-time-verify
content: CoreLink adapters verify PATs using `subtle::ConstantTimeEq` by reference (constant-time comparison to avoid timing side-channels).

label: corelink-audit-emitter-fail-closed
content: The CoreLink `AuditEmitter` trait is the canonical chokepoint surface that abstracts the audit-fail-CLOSED contract over any `AuditEvent`-shaped row.

label: corelink-cargo-adapter-no-upstream-fetch
content: The CoreLink cargo (sccache) adapter has no upstream fetch path, unlike the brew adapter, because sccache pushes build artifacts to the server (the adapter receives PUTs rather than fetching from an upstream domain).
quote: The cargo adapter is simpler than brew because it has no upstream fetch (sccache pushes artifacts to us)

label: corelink-axum-server-body-via-bodyext
content: For collecting incoming request bodies in CoreLink axum adapter servers, use `http_body_util::BodyExt` with `axum::body::Body` streaming rather than `futures_util`.
quote: revise the server to avoid `futures_util` by using `axum`'s body utilities instead

label: corelink-subtle-choice-unwrap-u8
content: In CoreLink's pinned `subtle` version, `ConstantTimeEq` returns a `Choice` that is not directly convertible to `u8`; convert it with `.unwrap_u8()`. Relates to [[corelink-pat-constant-time-verify]].
quote: The `subtle` version here returns `Choice` not directly convertible to `u8`. The correct API is `.unwrap_u8()`.

label: corelink-no-must-use-on-router
content: In CoreLink axum adapters, do not put `#[must_use]` on a function returning axum's `Router` (e.g. `build_router`) — `Router` is already `#[must_use]`, so clippy flags the redundant attribute under `-D warnings`.

label: corelink-unwrap-or-allowed-vs-bare-unwrap
content: CoreLink's zero-`unwrap()/expect()/panic!()` rule for `src/` bans only bare assertions. `unwrap_or(fallback)` is allowed in production code because it supplies a fallback rather than asserting; bare `unwrap()`/`panic!()` are confined to `#[cfg(test)]` blocks with `#[allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::panic)]`.

label: corelink-adapter-test-floor-10
content: CoreLink adapter crates have a test-count floor of ≥10 tests as a SEAL gate; the Wave-34 cargo adapter landed 34 tests (3.4× floor).
